chebyshev type-2 filters use a different frequency specification than most filters.  Rather than specifying the edge of the passband (where the signal falls to -3dB), you specify the edge of the stopband (where the filter first reaches the specified attenuation).
chebyshev type-1 filters provide a steep transition at a low computational cost.
butterworth filters provide a maximally-flat passband and a continuous transition toward negative infinity.

filterdesign dictionaries can be fed to a number of other objects in the Max environment.
zplane~ operates only on even-ordered filters, so for odd-ordered filters there will be an extra zero-pole pair located at the origin.
In this patcher, the difference in accuracy is shown, with the zpk representation plotted in blue and the transfer function represenation plotted in red.

The filterdesign object produces several filter representations, including the 64-bit coefficients for the transfer function of a single-section filter.  For low-order filters this often provides the most direct and convenient means of working.  As the order of the filters increase, the response of the filter becomes more sensitive to the limited numerical accuracy of the coefficients.  For this reason, it is most desirable to use a representation of the filter in terms of the location of its zeroes, poles, and gain (Z, P, and K).
